tactics.name: Heartbeat / health monitoring
tactics.move: Components emit liveness signals so failures are detected, not discovered.
tactics.appliesWhen: any component whose failure must be noticed within seconds

tactics.name: Standby (redundant spare)
tactics.move: A redundant instance takes over when the primary fails.
tactics.appliesWhen: single-instance services on the critical path
tactics.conditional: cost doubles for the protected component

tactics.name: Checkpoint / state snapshot
tactics.move: Periodic durable snapshots enable rollback and fast recovery.
tactics.appliesWhen: stateful components with recovery objectives

tactics.name: Comparator-checked redundancy
tactics.move: Independent computations compared to detect silent errors.
tactics.appliesWhen: computations where silent corruption is unacceptable (money movement, safety)
tactics.conditional: N-times compute cost; reserve for the truly critical

tactics.name: Retry with exponential backoff
tactics.move: Transient failures absorbed without amplifying incidents.
tactics.appliesWhen: every remote synchronous call

tactics.name: Timeout discipline
tactics.move: No call waits forever; budgets propagate down the chain.
tactics.appliesWhen: every remote call, budgeted from the user-facing SLO

tactics.name: Bulkhead isolation
tactics.move: Partition resources so one consumer's failure cannot exhaust the pool.
tactics.appliesWhen: shared services with heterogeneous consumers

tactics.name: Localize expected changes
tactics.move: Contain each anticipated change within one module boundary.
tactics.appliesWhen: requirements known to evolve (pricing rules, jurisdictions, product tiers)

tactics.name: Prevent ripple (intermediary)
tactics.move: An intermediary breaks direct dependency so change does not cascade.
tactics.appliesWhen: high fan-in components others depend on directly

tactics.name: Defer binding
tactics.move: Decisions moved from build time to config/runtime (flags, config, plugins).
tactics.appliesWhen: behavior that must vary per tenant, region or plan

tactics.name: Introduce caching
tactics.move: Serve repeated reads from a nearer, cheaper store.
tactics.appliesWhen: read-heavy paths with tolerable staleness
tactics.conditional: invalidation strategy is mandatory — a stale cache is a correctness bug

tactics.name: Increase concurrency
tactics.move: Parallelize independent work; remove serial bottlenecks.
tactics.appliesWhen: throughput-bound workloads with independent units

tactics.name: Shorten the critical path
tactics.move: Collapse or asynchronize hops on the latency-critical route.
tactics.appliesWhen: synchronous chains deeper than 3 on user-facing paths

tactics.name: Authorize at every boundary
tactics.move: Each trust boundary re-verifies identity and permission.
tactics.appliesWhen: every edge crossing a trust boundary

tactics.name: Encrypt in transit and at rest
tactics.move: Data protected on the wire and on disk; keys managed, rotated.
tactics.appliesWhen: any classified data flow or store

tactics.name: Least privilege
tactics.move: Every component holds only the permissions its function requires.
tactics.appliesWhen: always; verify at reviews

tactics.name: Tamper-evident audit trail
tactics.move: Security- and money-relevant actions leave an immutable record.
tactics.appliesWhen: regulated actions and administrative mutations

tactics.name: Horizontal scale-out
tactics.move: Stateless replicas behind a distributor absorb load linearly.
tactics.appliesWhen: load beyond one node; requires externalized state

tactics.name: Partition data
tactics.move: Shard by key so no single store is the ceiling.
tactics.appliesWhen: write volume beyond one primary
tactics.conditional: cross-partition queries and transactions become design work

tactics.name: Graceful degradation
tactics.move: Shed non-essential features to protect the core promise under stress.
tactics.appliesWhen: user-facing systems with distinguishable essential vs enhancement features
